newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST - Analysts see better B&O H1 96/97 result.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Analysts see better B&O H1 96/97 result.

text.p: Seven analysts polled by Reuters on Tuesday saw Danish upmarket audiomaker Bang & Olufsen (B&O) first half 1996/97 pre-tax and extraordinary items profits on average 30 percent up on the same period last year.

The panel forecast an average 166 million crown pre-tax and extraordinary interim profit for 1996/97 on 1.540 billion crown turnover, compared to 128 million crowns for 1995/96's first six months, when turnover was 1.335 billion crowns.
The estimates ranged from 165-167 million crowns.
The analysts' expectations for the half-year compared to B&O's own forecast of a 165 million crown pre-tax and minorities profit for the period.

For whole year 1996/97, the analysts predicted on average a pre-tax and extraordinary profit of 322 million crowns, with estimates between 272-345 million crowns, an 18 percent rise on 1995/96's full year 272 million crown surplus.
B&O issues its interim results on Wednesday January 29.
The share, which has risen over 30 percent in value since the company announced improved prospects last December, traded at 320, 12 crowns down on Monday's closing price, at 1100 gmt.
